For over 30 years, Angi has powered the future of the home services industry, creating an environment where homeowners and pros benefit from more jobs done well.

For homeowners, our platform is a reliable way to find skilled pros. For pros, we're a reliable business partner who helps them find the winnable work they want, when they want. For employees, we're an amazing place to call home. We can't wait to welcome you.

Angi at a glance:

  • Founded in 1995 as Angie’s List and rebranded in 2021

  • Global company with 9 brands in 8 countries and employees worldwide

  • Homeowners have turned to us for 300 million home projects and counting

About the role:

Angi’s Legal Department is seeking a Litigation and Risk Paralegal to join one of the most recognizable home services brands in North America. The team’s sole paralegal will have primary responsibility for investigation and response to escalated pre-litigation disputes. The position is fully remote, and will report to the SVP, Associate General Counsel of Angi. This role offers the opportunity to join the Legal team in a highly impactful, highly visible role.

Responsibilities:

PRE-LITIGATION DISPUTES AND REGULATORY INQUIRIES

  • Investigate and draft responses to escalated consumer complaints, including complaints filed with state attorneys general and complaints escalated to a consumer’s counsel

  • Investigate and draft responses to regulatory inquiries, including letters from state departments of labor and construction boards

  • Draft, maintain, and manage templates for escalated dispute letters

  • Develop and maintain processes and policies for managing escalated disputes in partnership with in-house counsel and the rest of the legal team

  • Maintain electronic records of pre-litigation disputes and regulatory matters within Angi’s matter management system

LITIGATION MATTERS

  • Assist with fact investigation to support ongoing litigation and intellectual property issues

  • Prepare and maintain electronic data for document production in litigation

  • Maintain electronic records of ongoing litigation within Angi’s matter management system

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree from four-year college or university, paralegal certification, or an equivalent combination of education and work experience

  • 7+ years’ experience as paralegal supporting litigation or dispute resolution required

  • Working knowledge of state and federal litigation procedure

  • Working knowledge of standard contractual language, including terms and conditions

  • Prior experience working in-house and/or at a law firm preferred

  • Must be able to communicate to cross-functional management in concise, easily understood terms

  • Ability to handle confidential data with appropriate discretion

  • Curiosity and willingness to learn and incorporate AI tools into daily legal work, such as using AI-assisted research, document review, or drafting tools to improve efficiency and accuracy

  • Top notch organizational skills; Proven ability to manage and meet reporting deadlines with quality, speed and accuracy

  • Strong work ethic and sense of accountability and integrity

  • Solid customer service focus and ability to work both independently and collaboratively with diverse teams across the organization

  • Self-starter, with a demonstrated ability to proactively identify issues, independently resolve problems and drive projects to completion

  • A creative problem solver who is comfortable with embracing and adopting new technology to assist with making work efficient and effective

Compensation & Benefits:

  • The base salary band for this position ranges from $75,000 - $120,000, commensurate with experience and performance. Compensation may vary based on factors such as geographic location

  • This position will be eligible for a competitive year end performance bonus & equity package

  • Full medical, dental, vision package to fit your needs

  • Flexible vacation policy; work hard and take time when you need it

  • Pet discount plans & retirement plan with company match (401K)

  • The rare opportunity to work at a technology company with sharp, motivated teammates solving some of the most unique challenges and changing the world

About AlphaSense:

AlphaSense is the AI platform redefining market intelligence and workflow orchestration, trusted by thousands of leading organizations to drive faster, more confident decisions in business and finance. The platform combines domain-specific AI with a vast content universe of over 500 million premium business documents — including equity research, earnings calls, expert interviews, filings, news, and internal proprietary content. Purpose-built for speed, accuracy, and enterprise-grade security, AlphaSense helps teams extract critical insights, uncover market-moving trends, and automate complex workflows with high-quality outputs. With AI solutions like Generative Search, Generative Grid, and Deep Research, AlphaSense delivers the clarity and depth professionals need to navigate complexity and obtain accurate, real-time information quickly. For more information, visit www.alpha-sense.com. Come join us.

About AlphaSense:

The world’s most sophisticated companies rely on AlphaSense to remove uncertainty from decision-making. With market intelligence and search built on proven AI, AlphaSense delivers insights that matter from content you can trust. Our universe of public and private content includes equity research, company filings, event transcripts, expert calls, news, trade journals, and clients’ own research content.

The acquisition of Tegus by AlphaSense in 2024 advances our shared mission to empower professionals to make smarter decisions through AI-driven market intelligence. Together, AlphaSense and Tegus will accelerate growth, innovation, and content expansion, with complementary product and content capabilities that enable users to unearth even more comprehensive insights from thousands of content sets. Our platform is trusted by over 4,000 enterprise customers, including a majority of the S&P 500. Founded in 2011, AlphaSense is headquartered in New York City with more than 2,500 employees across the globe and offices in the U.S., U.K., Finland, India, Singapore, Canada, and Ireland. Come join us!

About the Team:
AlphaSense has a great opportunity for a Contracts Manager to join our growing legal team. Legal is a critical function in supporting the company’s fast-paced environment and acts as a true business partner to all of our leaders across the organization. We work hand-in-hand with cross functional teams to provide solutions to enable and empower the company to achieve substantial growth targets while managing risk and protecting our business.

About the Role:

This role can either be based in our New York office or remotely in the United States. The Contracts Manager will primarily be responsible for reviewing various sales agreements and sales-related agreements. The Contracts Manager will report to the Managing Counsel, Commercial Contracts and will partner with other functions of the business (such as Product, Security, Privacy, Compliance, and Marketing) as necessary to help AlphaSense achieve its high-growth goals. This role is essential to our growth and will have an immediate impact in our dynamic, fast-paced culture.

Who You Are:

  • 4+ years’ experience with drafting and reviewing commercial agreements (with a heavy emphasis on sales agreements);
  • Ability to analyze and review a broad range of global sales contracts including Master Services Agreements, Order Forms, Statements of Work, Purchase Orders, Service Level Agreements, etc.;
  • Superior business acumen and a commitment to providing responsive support to our teams and to getting things done;
  • Experience managing a high volume of tasks for multiple stakeholders simultaneously and prioritizing based on greatest positive impact to the business;
  • Familiar with following and developing contracts playbooks;
  • Energetic and collaborative, with strong communication skills and a sense of humor;
  • Effective communicator with the ability to interact with both internal and external professionals of all types and backgrounds; and
  • Experience with contracting for artificial intelligence services, contract management systems and success in a high-growth tech environment are all a plus.

What You’ll Do:

  • Take ownership of reviewing, redlining, and negotiating sales contracts, escalating key issues to stakeholders as appropriate;
  • Collaborate with the company attorneys to ensure contracts reflect current legal and compliance requirements;
  • Partner cross-functionally to move deals efficiently through the sales cycle;
  • Help enhance and apply playbooks, policies, and processes to ensure consistency and conformance in contracts;
  • Manage operations, including workflow management and systems;
  • Provide general assistance to the AlphaSense legal team on contracts-related matters.

For base compensation, we set standard ranges for all roles based on function and level benchmarked against similar stage growth companies and internal comparables. In order to be compliant with local legislation, as well as to provide greater transparency to candidates, we share salary ranges on all job postings regardless of desired hiring location. Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors including candidate experience/expertise and may vary from the amounts listed below.

You may also be offered a performance-based bonus, equity, and a generous benefits program.

Base Compensation Range

$78,000—$108,000 USD

AlphaSense is an equal-opportunity employer. We are committed to a work environment that supports, inspires, and respects all individuals. All employees share in the responsibility for fulfilling AlphaSense’s commitment to equal employment opportunity. AlphaSense does not discriminate against any employee or applicant on the basis of race, color, sex (including pregnancy), national origin, age, religion, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, military or veteran status, disability, or any other non-merit factor. This policy applies to every aspect of employment at AlphaSense, including recruitment, hiring, training, advancement, and termination.

In addition, it is the policy of AlphaSense to provide reasonable accommodation to qualified employees who have protected disabilities to the extent required by applicable laws, regulations, and ordinances where a particular employee works.

Recruiting Scams and Fraud

We at AlphaSense have been made aware of fraudulent job postings and individuals impersonating AlphaSense recruiters. These scams may involve fake job offers, requests for sensitive personal information, or demands for payment. Please note:

  • AlphaSense never asks candidates to pay for job applications, equipment, or training.
  • All official communications will come from an @alpha-sense.com email address.
  • If you’re unsure about a job posting or recruiter, verify it on our Careers page.

If you believe you’ve been targeted by a scam or have any doubts regarding the authenticity of any job listing purportedly from or on behalf of AlphaSense please contact us. Your security and trust matter to us.

Why Socure?

Socure is building the identity trust infrastructure for the digital economy — verifying 100% of good identities in real time and stopping fraud before it starts. The mission is big, the problems are complex, and the impact is felt by businesses, governments, and millions of people every day.

We hire people who want that level of responsibility. People who move fast, think critically, act like owners, and care deeply about solving customer problems with precision. If you want predictability or narrow scope, this won’t be your place. If you want to help build the future of identity with a team that holds a high bar for itself — keep reading.

As Identity Product Counsel, you’ll partner with our computer vision and AI innovators to develop and launch new digital identity and fraud prevention products. You will participate throughout the product development lifecycle to advise on legal risks, establish compliance controls, and support entry to new and global markets. Socure is an ambitious, high-growth company, so you will immediately see the impact of your contributions.


The Role:

  • Provide legal guidance to product, data science, engineering, and sales/marketing teams on the development of our document verification and digital intelligence products. You’ll touch a wide range of laws, including privacy (especially biometrics), consumer protection, responsible AI, age assurance, and laws that regulate identity cards, numbers and authoritative data sources. You’ll also advise on model risk, machine learning bias, fair lending, and accessibility. You’ll get familiar with official privacy and identity standards relevant to government procurement and global markets.

  • Take a risk-based and business enabling approach. You will closely track our company and product strategies in order to manage and minimize legal risks. Maintain documentation so your guidance is easy to implement.

  • Advise on the commercial terms (customer and vendor agreements) that affect our products.

  • Draft terms of use, product and privacy policies, disclosures, customer documentation, and implement related processes.

  • Review external communications about our products, including to customers, the market, regulators, and the press.

  • Work with a dynamic and lean team of product and regulatory legal experts who are always in the middle of stimulating and novel issues. You also will be the product expert for the Legal and our Government Affairs teams, as needed to support their work in contracting, corporate and regulatory matters.

  • Partner with Data Acquisition & Licensing and Commercial Legal to ensure that data sources and customer contract terms for DocV and Digital Intelligence align with Socure's rights and restrictions, and that novel requirements are built into contract templates and negotiation playbooks.

  • Participate in Socure's privacy and data governance programs, including privacy-by-design reviews, data protection impact assessments, regulatory monitoring, and consumer-facing issues.

  • Support customer and prospect engagement as a subject-matter expert, including regulator, bank-partner, and customer due diligence, security and compliance questionnaires, and regulated-industry go-to-market efforts.

  • Handle government and regulator discussions and disclosures on compliance readiness, in coordination with Government Affairs and external counsel.

  • Use AI tools as part of your everyday legal workflow, including AI-assisted drafting, research, and review. Surface and help build ideas for automating repeatable legal processes.

  • Design training and sales-enablement resources on key legal issues for general and targeted audiences.

  • Monitor legal developments, and offer creative, pragmatic ideas on how the company can work within the law to pursue innovation and competitive advantage.

  • Special projects as they may arise in your areas of expertise.


What you Bring:

  • 3-5+ years of combined, relevant experience, including experience at a law firm and/or in-house for a financial institution or fintech

  • Technical background in engineering, computer science, data analytics, statistics, or related areas

  • Familiarity with launching products and advising on the legal and regulatory implications of technology products

  • Familiarity with state and federal privacy and AI laws

  • Fluency translating legal advice into actionable guidance for innovative product and business teams

  • Avid interest in progressing your legal, tech and commercial knowledge, and evolving your skills in communication and advocacy

  • Ability to organize, prioritize, and manage projects effectively

  • Sound and practical business judgment, intellectual creativity, and communication and problem-solving skills

  • A JD and active membership in at least one state bar

Socure is an equal opportunity employer that values diversity in all its forms within our company. We do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.
If you need an accommodation during any stage of the application or hiring process—including interview or onboarding support—please reach out to your Socure recruiting partner directly.

About Stripe

Stripe is a technology company that builds financial infrastructure for the internet. Millions of businesses, from startups to global enterprises, use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and expand into new markets. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet.

Our products support a broad range of business needs, from payments and software services to emerging areas such as stablecoins and agentic commerce.

About the role

We’re looking for an experienced transactional lawyer to join our Commercial Legal team supporting Stripe’s business in the Americas. You’ll lead complex commercial negotiations, advise on new products and international expansion, and help build the legal processes and tools that support Stripe’s growth.

You’ll work closely with Sales, Product Legal, and teams across Stripe to solve challenging problems and provide practical advice. You’ll also help improve how the Commercial Legal team works, including through the use of AI tools.

What you’ll do

  • Support the Americas Sales team and lead negotiations for complex and strategic commercial agreements.
  • Advise on commercial and legal issues related to new product launches and international expansion.
  • Partner with Product Legal to bring new products and features to market.
  • Draft and maintain agreements and playbooks, improve internal processes, and use AI tools to help the team work more effectively with colleagues, partners, and users.
  • Collaborate with teams globally, including Sales, Operations, Product, Tax, and Risk.
  • Help the global Commercial Legal team deliver consistent, efficient support as Stripe grows.
  • Develop and deliver training and resources that help the Sales team understand and sell Stripe’s products.
  • Serve as a point of escalation for outside counsel.

Who you are

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements below. If you do, we encourage you to apply. Preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • A Juris Doctor (JD) degree or foreign equivalent, and membership in good standing in at least one U.S. state bar.
  • At least 8 years of relevant legal experience, either in-house or in the technology practice of a leading law firm.
  • Familiarity with the legal issues and commercial risks associated with hosted data and technology services.
  • Intellectual curiosity and creative problem-solving skills, with an interest in learning complex, evolving products and finding practical solutions.
  • A proactive approach and a strong sense of ownership.
  • Clear, concise written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex issues and key risks in plain language.
  • The ability to guide cross-functional teams toward solutions that address business needs and legal risks.
  • A collaborative approach and a willingness to contribute to the team’s shared success.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience in payments or financial technology, including familiarity with related regulatory issues.
  • In-house experience advising high-growth companies.
  • Working knowledge of large language model (LLM) tools.
  • Experience using AI technology to improve legal processes.
  • Working knowledge of data protection laws such as the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA), the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), and the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA).

Joining Collibra’s Legal team

Collibra is seeking a Commercial Counsel to join our high-impact Legal team. You will be a key individual responsible for drafting, negotiating, and closing enterprise SaaS, software, and technology-related agreements that power Collibra's growth. You will also spend part of your time working on privacy matters. This role provides critical legal and commercial support to our Sales and Procurement organizations, ensuring Collibra continues to close deals quickly while staying protected on risk, compliance, and contractual terms. You will act as a trusted legal partner to the business, working closely with Sales, Finance, Security, and Procurement to move deals forward without cutting corners on legal protection.

Commercial Counsels at Collibra are responsible for

  • Drafting, reviewing, and negotiating enterprise SaaS, software, and technology agreements including partnership, reseller, supply, and licensing agreements to support Collibra's commercial relationships.
  • Managing the commercial contracting process to keep deals moving efficiently while protecting Collibra's legal interests.
  • Partnering with Sales, Sales Operations, Finance, Security, and Procurement teams to drive transactions to successful completion.
  • Advising on the structure of customer arrangements to support sound legal and business decisions.
  • Negotiating data processing agreements, security addenda, AI addenda, and privacy terms with customers and vendors, and advising on how data flows through Collibra’s platform.
  • Monitoring regulatory and legal developments, and advising on related legal matters arising from Collibra's operations, to help the company stay ahead of compliance requirements.

You have

  • 5+ years of relevant legal experience, preferably as in-house commercial contracts counsel in the software industry.
  • A J.D. and active admission to practice law in at least one U.S. state, in good standing.
  • Hands-on privacy experience in a SaaS context, including negotiating DPAs, and working knowledge of U.S. state privacy laws (such as CCPA/CPRA), GDPR, and international data transfer mechanisms. A privacy certification (CIPP/US or CIPP/E) is a plus.
  • Demonstrated proficiency in leveraging AI tools (e.g., Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT, Harvey) to solve real-world business challenges, drive measurable outcomes, and streamline workflows.
  • Experience negotiating with large enterprise or public sector customers.
  • Demonstrated proficiency in leveraging AI tools (e.g., Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT, Copilot) to solve real-world business challenges, drive measurable outcomes, or streamline workflows.
  • A bachelor’s degree or equivalent related working experience is required.
  • This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship.

You are

  • Applying strong drafting and negotiation skills, grounded in excellent business judgment and critical thinking.
  • Attending to detail, catching nuances in complex commercial agreements.
  • Communicator with a service-oriented approach, building trusted relationships with legal and non-legal colleagues.
  • Someone who prioritizes and manages multiple tasks and stakeholders simultaneously.
  • Taking initiative, identifying and acting on opportunities without waiting for direction.

Measures of success

  • Within your first month, you will get familiar with Collibra's product, contracting processes, and risk appetite.
  • Within your third month, you will independently negotiate contracts with enterprise customers and partners.

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. This role will support Bridge as it develops and scales products for companies operating across markets.

StackAdapt is a remote first company. This role is open to applicants currently located in Canada or the United States.

About Dojo

Dojo started as a simple way for teachers to show parents what happened in class. Today it's used in 95% of US K-8 schools and by 1 in 4 American families, and reaches about 50 million kids in 180 countries. We got here with around 220 people and have never paid for a user.

Families trust us with their kids, and we're now building on that trust. On Dojo Islands, kids explore a shared world with their friends after school. Dojo Tutor connects families with tutors. Sparks is an AI tutor for every kid, and Login with Dojo will let children sign in safely anywhere online.

Our mission is to give every child on Earth an education they love. We hire for talent density, and many of our people came from Instagram, Netflix, Dropbox, Stripe, Uber and Y Combinator.

The job

Every product above lives in a category whose rules haven't been written yet. State legislatures, the FTC and the EU are writing them right now. What should a shared online world for eight-year-olds allow? How should an AI talk to a child? Who verifies a kid's identity, and what happens to that data? Some company will answer these questions well, in public, and earn the trust of parents and schools for a generation. We want that company to be Dojo, and we want you to lead it.

As Head of Legal you'll sit on the leadership team and work directly with our co-founders. You'll own all of legal: product, privacy, commercial, corporate, employment, IP, regulatory and litigation. You'll inherit good foundations, including a small in-house team, trusted outside counsel and working commercial and privacy processes. Your job is to make them great.

We have strong views on how this should work. Trust is our moat, and the right Head of Legal makes it deeper every quarter while teams ship faster. The best legal answer is usually a version of yes with sensible guardrails, reached early, before anyone has spent months building the wrong thing. We also think AI now lets a small team of exceptional lawyers do what used to take fifteen. You'll get to prove it.

Your first 18 months

Make Dojo the company parents trust most with their kids.

  • Decide where Dojo stands on the hardest questions in kids' tech, and say it publicly before regulators decide for us: AI that talks to children, kids playing together online, and how products for kids should make money.

  • Figure out which seals and certifications actually change a parent's or a district's mind, then win them.

  • Make privacy one of the reasons districts pick Dojo.

  • When a regulator calls, handle it so well that the product and our reputation come out unharmed.

Make legal the reason things ship faster.

  • Get pulled into the room early by product, engineering and partnerships, because you make their plans better. Find the version that can ship, name the one or two real showstoppers, and tell the team what to do this week.

  • Turn standard contracts in hours and product questions in two days.

  • Write the playbooks that let district data agreements, partnerships and vendor deals close without starting from zero each time.

Build a legal team that outperforms teams five times its size.

  • Lead and grow a small, very good in-house team, and hold outside counsel to budget and to your standard.

  • Put AI into the daily work on contracts, data agreements and privacy reviews. Decide what comes in-house and what stays with specialists, so outside spend falls while quality rises.

  • Own M&A, financing and board matters with our CFO, and keep the company ready to do a deal or a raise on short notice.

You will be a match if:

  • You've led legal at a consumer tech company of 100 to 1,000 people, where product and engineering create most of the value.

  • Product and business leaders who've worked with you say, unprompted, that you made them faster and found answers they hadn't seen. You end your advice with what you'd do, and once the call is made you own it.

  • You've owned privacy for a consumer product, ideally one for kids, across COPPA, FERPA, state student privacy laws, CCPA/CPRA, GDPR and the new rules on AI. If your depth is narrower, you learn fast and already think about it clearly.

  • You're comfortable running M&A, financings and board work alongside a CFO.

  • You've led talent-dense teams and managed several outside firms to budget. You know the right specialist for almost any problem and can get them on the phone today.

  • You've rebuilt legal work with AI yourself, and can explain concretely how three lawyers plus specialists can match fifteen.

  • You turn a messy problem into the two or three decisions that matter, and you write short. You hold a position without starting a war, and you change your mind when the facts change, and you move decisions on trust rather than title.

  • You move fast enough to make people slightly nervous, and you raise the bar on ambition as much as on rigor.

Bonus:

  • 10+ years in law, ideally including child-directed products or student data.

  • Time spent in strategy consulting, operating, finance or engineering.

  • You've stepped into an existing legal function and made it markedly better, or led a distributed team.

  • You can tell Dojo's story to a regulator, a reporter or a partner and leave them on our side.

You won't match every line here. If these problems make you want to start tomorrow, apply anyway. Some of our best people took unusual paths to get here.

Why now

Very few legal jobs let you shape how a generation of kids experiences the internet. The questions are new, the stakes are real, and the answers you reach here will set norms far beyond Dojo. You'll have the scale to matter, a team small enough that your judgment shows up in everything, and founders who want a real partner on the hardest calls.

Who We Are

At OKX, we believe that the future will be reshaped by crypto, and ultimately contribute to every individual's freedom. OKX is a leading crypto exchange, and the developer of OKX Wallet, giving millions access to crypto trading and decentralized crypto applications (dApps). OKX is also a trusted brand by hundreds of large institutions seeking access to crypto markets. We are safe and reliable, backed by our Proof of Reserves. Across our multiple offices globally, we are united by our core principles: We Before Me, Do the Right Thing, and Get Things Done. These shared values drive our culture, shape our processes, and foster a friendly, rewarding, and diverse environment for every OK-er.

About the Opportunity

The Americas Compliance team is hiring a Senior Compliance Manager to own compliance for OKXICE TSV. OKXICE TSV is the tokenized securities venue run by the OKX and Intercontinental Exchange joint venture under the SEC's Innovation Exemption, and it lets eligible US users trade tokenized US-listed stocks on-chain. You'll be the main person accountable for meeting the exemption's ongoing conditions. You'll work closely with Legal, Product, Web3 Risk Control and our AML, Sanctions and Surveillance teams. This is a new role on a new type of venue, so you'll help build the program as well as run it.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Own the compliance program for the venue's SEC exemption, including tracking each condition, testing controls and keeping records ready for regulatory examination.

  • Manage the venue's public notice: review revisions, control versions, and make sure the notice matches how the product actually works. This includes corrections and material-change filings within the required deadlines.

  • Run the issuer notice process from start to finish, including tracking delivery, handling objections and confirming each stock's listing date.

  • Track and monitor TSV limits on an ongoing basis, including per-stock and volume limits against consolidated market data, periodic tier rechecks, trading halts and eligible stablecoins. Escalate breaches, significant operational events and required SEC notifications.

  • Oversee participant onboarding and ongoing wallet maintenance and monitoring, including KYC/KYB, daily sanctions and on-chain wallet rescreening, keeping wallet-to-participant records current, and issuing and revoking the soulbound token (SBT) credential that grants access.

  • Report to the OKXICE LLC Board of Managers and to Americas Compliance leadership, and manage and develop a TSV Compliance Analyst.

What We Look For In You

  • 8+ years of compliance experience at a broker-dealer, exchange, alternative trading system (ATS) or digital asset firm, with direct experience of SEC-regulated activity.

  • Working knowledge of the federal securities laws that apply to trading venues, such as Regulation ATS, Regulation NMS and market manipulation rules, plus the ability to apply them to new market structures.

  • Experience building or running compliance programs under regulatory conditions, exemptive relief or no-action positions.

  • Familiarity with how blockchain-based trading works, including self-custodied wallets, smart contracts, liquidity pools and on-chain screening.

  • Strong drafting skills, with experience turning complex technical or legal detail into clear public disclosures and procedures.

  • Sound judgment and the ability to work with Product, Engineering and Legal teams across time zones.

Nice to Haves

  • Experience with tokenized securities, transfer agents or digital asset broker-dealers.

  • Exposure to OFAC sanctions programs and blocked property handling for on-chain assets.

  • Experience reporting to a board or joint venture governance body.

  • A JD or a similar legal background.

Perks & Benefits

  • Various team building programs and company events

  • Wellness and meal allowances

  • Comprehensive healthcare schemes for employees and dependants

About the role:

Mercury is looking for a Model Risk Manager to help build and operate a practical, risk-based Model Risk Management program as we continue to scale and prepare for life as a regulated bank.

Models support an increasingly broad range of decisions across Mercury, including credit underwriting, portfolio management, fraud prevention, BSA/AML, CECL, finance, liquidity, pricing, and operational processes. This role will provide independent review and effective challenge throughout the model lifecycle while helping Mercury apply governance proportionate to the actual risk of each model.

This is a hands-on role for someone who can move comfortably between technical analysis, regulatory expectations, and business context. You will conduct model validations, challenge assumptions and limitations, improve our model inventory and monitoring practices, and work closely with teams across Risk Ops, Data, Engineering, Product, Finance, Compliance, and Internal Audit.

Showing up as a true collaborator, advisor and partner to the business will be key as we continue to build out this function and work towards our collective goals at Mercury. You should be comfortable operating in a fast-moving environment where the objective is not governance for its own sake, but helping Mercury use models safely, responsibly, and effectively.

What you’ll do:

  • Perform independent validations and reviews of internally developed and third-party models across areas such as credit, fraud, BSA/AML, CECL, finance, liquidity, pricing, and operational risk.
  • Evaluate each model’s methodology, assumptions, data quality and lineage, implementation, and performance through reviews and testings such as outcomes analysis, benchmarking, back-testing, and sensitivity testing scaled to its risk and materiality.
  • Provide credible and constructive challenges to model developers, owners, and users while maintaining effective working relationships with 1LOD.
  • Assess model risk and materiality based on a model’s inherent risk, purpose, exposure, use, and potential impact.
  • Help maintain a complete and accurate model inventory, including model ownership, risk rating, dependencies, limitations, validation status, monitoring requirements, and open issues.
  • Review ongoing monitoring plans and results, including performance thresholds, overrides, data drift, model changes, and conditions that could make a model no longer fit for purpose.
  • Evaluate vendor models and other third-party analytical products, including available documentation, transparency, performance, limitations, customization, and Mercury’s ability to monitor and control their use.
  • Document validation conclusions clearly, identify issues, recommend proportionate remediation, and track findings through resolution.
  • Support controlled model use when validation cannot be completed before implementation by helping establish appropriate limitations, compensating controls, monitoring, and approvals.
  • Develop clear reporting on model risk, validation coverage, performance concerns, concentrations, dependencies, exceptions, and overdue remediation for management and governance committees.
  • Help improve Mercury’s Model Risk Management Policy, standards, procedures, and templates.
  • Use automation and analytical tools to make model inventory management, testing, monitoring, and reporting more efficient.
  • Partner with Mercury’s Data and AI Governance teams to establish clear boundaries and handoffs between traditional model risk management and the governance of generative AI, agentic AI, and other analytical systems outside the formal model definition.
  • Support regulatory examinations, Internal Audit reviews, and other assurance activities involving model risk.

What we’re looking for:

  • 5+ years of relevant experience in model validation, model development, quantitative risk analytics, or a related discipline within banking, fintech, financial services, or consulting.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Physics, Computer Science, Engineering, Financial Engineering or a related field. Master’s degree or PhD is preferred.
  • Strong knowledge of model risk management principles and current regulatory expectations, including the revised interagency guidance reflected in SR 26-2.
  • Intensive experience validating or developing models in one or more areas such as BSA/AML, fraud, financial forecasting, CECL, capital, liquidity, and credit underwriting, using one or more methodologies such as machine learning (e.g., XGBoost, random forests), scorecards, complex vendor models (e.g., Alloy, Firco), and complex spreadsheet-based models.
  • Proficiency with SQL and Python (from a data analytics lens); comfortable building understanding of models independently of their developers through collecting evidence and data analytics.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills; you can explain model risk to a data scientist and to a regulator, or translate your findings and recommendations to guidance for the 1LOD product/business teams, and use different language for each.
  • Exceptional attention to detail across documentation, code base, testing artifacts and quantitative analysis provided by 1LOD.
  • Sound judgment and a practical, risk-based mindset: you can distinguish significant model risk from lower-risk matters and have the confidence to challenge model owners constructively, including senior stakeholders.
  • High ownership, intellectual curiosity, and comfort building processes in a fast evolving environment, where priorities evolve quickly, new ad hoc requests emerge regularly, and role boundaries are intentionally broad. You can operate effectively without tightly-defined scope, find the highest-leverage work, and get it done.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Experience helping build or materially enhance a model risk management program.
  • Familiarity with bank regulatory examinations, charter readiness, or the implementation of risk programs within a growing financial institution.
  • Knowledge of Haskell

What success looks like:

  • Mercury maintains a complete and reliable view of its material models and aggregate model risk.
  • Critical models receive timely, technically credible, and risk-based independent review.
  • Model limitations, performance concerns, and remediation needs are clearly understood and acted upon.
  • Model owners view Model Risk as a rigorous and constructive partner that improves decisions without creating unnecessary friction.
  • Mercury’s Model Risk Management program is scalable, practical, and ready to withstand regulatory and independent assurance review.

About the role:

As Mercury continues its rapid growth trajectory, navigating an increasingly complex regulatory, partner, and product landscape is critical. Compliance is not only a requirement, but a competitive advantage that enables Mercury to move faster, build trust, and launch innovative products responsibly.

Nowhere is that more true than in AI. We believe we have a path to lead the US banking* industry into the AI era, and that how we choose to build and deploy AI will define our success over the next three years.

We are building first-party agentic products, headless and agent-accessible banking through our API and MCP, and the internal platforms that let us build with AI at speed. Core to all of it is great governance—these systems must run on one trusted system of access, logging, and data controls that meets the requirements of our banking ambitions.

We are seeking a Lead Compliance Risk Manager to serve as the compliance advisor for Mercury's AI products. This is a new, high-visibility role and the first dedicated compliance advisory seat covering AI at Mercury. You will be the leading authority on AI product compliance risk for the Compliance Team—shaping how we build, how we govern, and how we explain ourselves to our partners and regulators.

You will partner closely with Product, Engineering, Risk, Data, Legal, and Operations to ensure Mercury's AI products are compliant-by-design from concept through launch and scale. You will also help define the AI governance framework itself: the standards, controls, escalation paths, and documentation that allow a bank-partnered fintech to deploy agentic capabilities responsibly and at pace.

How this role fits alongside our other AI roles: this is a product compliance advisory role. Our Data & AI Governance team owns enterprise governance frameworks, responsible-AI standards, AI use case intake and inventory, and risk classification; Model Risk Management owns model inventory, tiering, and validation. You will be a close partner to and a major consumer of both—running our AI products through their processes, applying their standards to real product decisions, and bringing them the product-level detail they need to see. You will also help extend our existing product compliance playbooks to cover AI features, in partnership with your manager and the rest of the Product Compliance team. Your mandate is the products, not the program.

In this role, you will:

  • Serve as the subject matter expert and primary compliance advisor for Mercury's AI and agentic products, including Command, our API, and agentic access methods such as MCP and CLI.
  • Work closely with cross-functional risk and product teams to bring Mercury's AI products to market in a way that meets all relevant financial partner, regulatory compliance obligations, and our AI governance standards.
  • Ensure all processes and products under your area of responsibility comply with applicable rules and regulations. Stay up to date with changes to applicable regulations, supervisory guidance, and emerging AI-specific law, and implement necessary updates to impacted products to maintain compliance.
  • Support expansion for new product launches by scoping, defining, and communicating product and compliance requirements.
  • Work cross-functionally to drive remediation efforts for products within your defined scope.
  • Support the compliance function in defining and achieving departmental initiatives, maintaining relevant policies and procedures, developing documentation solutions, and liaising with auditors.
  • Mentor and provide strategic guidance to compliance colleagues as AI capabilities spread across every product domain, and contribute to building a strong culture of compliance across Mercury.
  • Work closely with our Risk team, which owns AI governance, as Compliance’s AI product expert to contribute product-level guidance to ongoing AI governance updates.

Core responsibilities:

  • Partner closely with Product, Engineering, Risk, Data, Operations, and Legal to bring Mercury's AI products to market in a manner that meets all relevant regulatory, financial partner, and network obligations.
  • Advise product and engineering teams throughout the product lifecycle—discovery, design, evaluation, launch, and iteration—to ensure AI products are compliant-by-design rather than reviewed after the fact.
  • Identify, assess, and document compliance risks specific to AI and agentic systems—including inaccurate or fabricated output, unauthorized or over-scoped agent action, inadequate consent and disclosure, unexplainable decisioning, disparate impact, data leakage across customers or organizations, prompt injection and third-party agent risk, and insufficient audit trail—and work cross-functionally to design pragmatic mitigation strategies.
  • Define the compliance requirements for the platforms AI is built on, in partnership with the teams that own them: the LLM gateway all internal traffic routes through, the internal app platform, agent orchestration frameworks, and the data access and governance layer.
  • Establish and refine AI-specific compliance standards for the department—what evidence a launch requires, what must be logged, what requires human review, what must be escalated, and what is out of bounds—and ensure those standards evolve as the organization and the technology grow.
  • Support new product launches and expansions by scoping, defining, and communicating compliance requirements clearly and early, including for co-marketing and distribution partnerships with third-party AI platforms.
  • Monitor regulatory, supervisory, and industry developments relevant to AI in financial services, assess impact, and drive implementation of required changes.
  • Own and oversee multiple concurrent high-impact AI compliance workstreams, holding project owners accountable for results and ensuring each aligns with department and company objectives.
  • Support remediation efforts for products within scope, including root cause analysis, corrective action planning, and execution tracking.
  • Partner with executive leadership, partner bank compliance teams, and external advisors to guide high-level decisions on AI direction, presenting data-driven recommendations.
  • Contribute to the broader Compliance function by supporting policy development, documentation standards, audit preparation, and examiner interactions.
  • Help build and reinforce a strong culture of compliance across Mercury through collaboration, education, and influence—including raising the AI fluency of the Compliance team itself, and developing scalable tools, templates, and frameworks others can reuse.

You should have:

  • 8+ years of experience in a compliance advisory, product compliance, or regulatory risk role, ideally within fintech or financial services, with a track record of being the recognized authority in your domain.
  • Demonstrated experience advising on AI, machine learning, or model-driven products in a regulated environment—or comparable experience standing up a new compliance domain where no playbook existed.
  • Working knowledge of the regulatory and supervisory framework relevant to AI in banking, including UDAAP, fair lending and ECOA/Reg B, FCRA and adverse action, Reg E and payments authorization, BSA/AML, GLBA and privacy, marketing and disclosure requirements, recordkeeping, complaint management, model risk management expectations, and third-party and vendor risk management guidance.
  • Familiarity with emerging AI-specific regimes and frameworks and the ability to form a practical view on their application—such as the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, state AI and automated decisioning laws.
  • Technical fluency to engage credibly with engineers on model behavior, evaluation and testing, agent permissioning and tool scoping, logging and observability, and data access controls—and to know which questions actually surface risk.
  • Deep experience partnering with product and engineering teams on regulatory and compliance matters across the product lifecycle, including on fast-moving launches with external dependencies.
  • Proven ability to own highly ambiguous, large-scale compliance problems and to create and execute a strategy to address them, without waiting for precedent.
  • Experience designing compliance frameworks that span multiple product lines or departments, and improving systems and processes so that compliance posture evolves alongside business growth.
  • Demonstrated success operating with senior stakeholders, including executives, partner banks, auditors, or regulators, and presenting data-driven recommendations that drive decisions.
  • Strong project management skills, including the ability to define problems, create execution plans, manage several high-impact initiatives at once, and drive outcomes.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate regulatory and financial partner risk into terms stakeholder teams understand, and to resolve conflict around risk tolerance, resourcing, and timelines.
  • Experience mentoring mid-level compliance professionals and raising the capability of a team, not just delivering your own work.
  • Comfort operating independently in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment, with sound judgment on when to move and when to escalate.
  • Curiosity, adaptability, and genuine interest in engaging with frontier technology and the regulatory challenges that come with it.

jobs.jobDescription:
Clover Health is investing in our fraud detection and investigation capabilities and is seeking a Director, AI-Enabled Fraud Prevention & Investigations to join our Legal department as a senior individual contributor. This hybrid role combines: (1) managing hands-on investigations of potential provider fraud with (2) building AI-powered tools and processes to make investigations more efficient and help catch potential future fraud earlier. You will develop and pilot new AI-enabled investigatory processes for Clover’s Medicare Advantage business, and own resulting investigations, in collaboration with Clover’s Special Investigations Unit (SIU) and other stakeholders.

This is a non-attorney role. You will work hand-in-hand with Clover’s lawyers and SIU to ensure that new investigatory processes you develop, and the resulting investigations, comply with Clover policies and regulatory requirements. Success in this role requires someone sharp, creative, and technically hands-on—someone who does not just use existing analytics tools but builds their own. That might mean writing a script to automate repetitive work, pulling apart a dataset when a standard report falls short, or working with an LLM until it produces something genuinely useful—all with the goal of finding smarter, more effective ways to investigate potential provider fraud.

As a Director, AI-Enabled Fraud Prevention & Investigations, you will:

  • Build Your Own Investigative Tooling: Use AI to write the queries, scripts, and prompts that turn millions of claim lines and/or medical record data into a prioritized list of leads. Prototype detection logic yourself rather than waiting on a roadmap, and hand off what works to data science and engineering to productionize. We expect you to be the person who builds v1.
  • Investigate Potential Fraud End-to-End With AI in the Loop: Own a portfolio of fraud investigations sourced using the tooling you develop, in collaboration with Clover’s SIU. Develop investigative plans, gather and analyze evidence (including claims data and medical records), and reach well-supported conclusions. Use LLMs and analytics to compress the parts of an investigation that have always been slow — reading unstructured data, triaging grievance narratives, and sizing exposure.
  • Build Defensible Documentation: Develop case files and memos that are factually complete, well-organized, and prepared with the evidentiary and procedural standards necessary for downstream enforcement, recoveries, or provider actions.
  • Collaborate Across Functions: Work with Clover's clinical, compliance, claims, payment integrity, provider relations, revenue operations, and SIU teams to gather information, validate findings, and translate investigative outcomes into operational improvements, provider education, and member impact.
  • Communicate Findings Clearly: Prepare concise written reports and oral briefings that translate complex investigative facts into clear narratives for senior leadership and other stakeholders.

Success in this role looks like:

  • In your first 90 days, you have embedded yourself as a trusted partner to both the Legal department and Clover’s SIU. You have built working relationships with key stakeholders across Clover's clinical, compliance, claims, payment integrity, revenue operations, and legal teams, and you have begun working through your initial portfolio of fraud investigations and ad hoc referrals.
  • By 6 months, you are independently managing a steady caseload of fraud investigations with consistently high-quality work product, in collaboration with SIU. You have a clear working rhythm with Legal and SIU, and you have built at least one working tool — a script, a notebook, a dashboard, a prompt.
  • By 12 months, you have a track record of strong investigations, successful recoveries and/or referrals, and effective cross-functional collaboration. Senior leaders across Clover view you as a trusted person to call when they have a hunch that something doesn't look right and want it examined.

You should get in touch if:

  • Knowledge of healthcare fraud schemes & investigative experience: You have experience in healthcare fraud investigations, program integrity, or SIU operations, ideally within Medicare Advantage or managed care. You understand healthcare fraud schemes and know how to use claims data, medical records, and provider documentation to build a defensible factual record.
  • You are AI-native and enjoy building things using LLMs: You can use LLMs to write SQL, Python, etc., to interrogate large claims and/or medical record datasets, automate investigative work, and prototype your own solutions rather than waiting for someone else to build them. We do not expect production-grade engineering or require formal technical training—we value demonstrated ability to build, ship, and showcase solutions that work.
  • Strong communication skills: You are a strong writer and communicator who can turn complex investigative findings into clear memos, referrals, and executive summaries, and you are comfortable building in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment.

Bonus points if:

    • You have built something people actually use—an internal tool, detection model, script, automation, or AI workflow that made a manual process better. We would rather see something scrappy and useful in production than something polished in a slide.
    • You have hands-on experience applying AI/ML to fraud, investigations, or compliance.
    • You have a J.D., legal training, or experience working alongside Legal, SIU, or compliance at a health plan.
    • You have industry certifications such as CFE, AHFI, or CHC.

Benefits Overview:

  • Financial Well-Being: Our commitment to attracting and retaining top talent begins with a competitive base salary and equity opportunities. Additionally, we offer a performance-based bonus program, 401k matching, and regular compensation reviews to recognize and reward exceptional contributions.
  • Physical Well-Being: We prioritize the health and well-being of our employees and their families by providing comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage. Your health matters to us, and we invest in ensuring you have access to quality healthcare.

To support this, we offer initiatives such as No-Meeting Fridays, monthly company holidays, access to mental health resources, and a generous flexible time-off policy. Additionally, we embrace a remote-first culture that supports collaboration and flexibility, allowing our team members to thrive from any location.
  • Professional Development: Developing internal talent is a priority for Clover. We offer learning programs, mentorship, professional development funding, and regular performance feedback and reviews.

Additional Perks:

  • Reimbursement for office setup expenses

  • Remote-first culture, enabling collaboration with global teams
  • Paid parental leave for all new parents

We believe the healthcare system is broken, so we've created custom software and analytics to empower our clinical staff to intervene and provide personalized care to the people who need it most.

We always put our members first, and our success as a team is measured by the quality of life of the people we serve. Those who work at Clover are passionate and mission-driven individuals with diverse areas of expertise, working together to solve the most complicated problem in the world: healthcare.

Diversity not only includes race and gender identity, but also age, disability status, veteran status, sexual orientation, religion and many other parts of one’s identity. jobs.jobDescription:
About the Role

Dispatch is looking for a Head of Legal to own the day-to-day legal function at Dispatch.

This is a highly hands-on role for an experienced commercial attorney who is comfortable operating as an individual contributor, making practical risk decisions, and building the legal infrastructure of an early-stage company. You will work closely with our Sales, Customer Success, Product, Security, Finance, People, and executive teams, with particular responsibility for enterprise commercial agreements, privacy and data matters, and the legal processes that support our growth.

The ideal candidate combines strong law firm training with meaningful in-house experience at an early-stage (Series C or earlier) B2B SaaS company. You should be equally comfortable negotiating a complex enterprise agreement, advising the business on a new data-sharing arrangement, and creating the templates and playbooks that allow the company to move faster without introducing unnecessary risk.

This role reports to the COO and is an individual contributor position initially with the expectation of growing and scaling the team over time.

Fundraising, investor matters and other specialized corporate matters will continue to be handled by outside counsel.

How You'll Operate

This role is designed for someone who likes being close to the business.

You will handle the company's highest-volume and highest-impact legal work, create repeatable systems where they do not yet exist, and know when an issue warrants escalation to specialized outside counsel.

Success in this role means helping Dispatch move quickly while making thoughtful, commercially grounded decisions about risk. The goal is not to eliminate risk; it is to make sure the company understands it, takes it deliberately, and builds the processes needed to scale.

What You'll Own

Commercial Contracts

  • Own the commercial contracting function, including drafting, reviewing, and negotiating MSAs, order forms, amendments, statements of work, and multi-year enterprise agreements.

  • Lead negotiations with sophisticated enterprise customers and their legal, procurement, privacy, and security teams.

  • Develop pragmatic positions on indemnification, limitations of liability, warranties, insurance, intellectual property, termination rights, service levels, and other material commercial terms.

  • Partner closely with Sales and company leadership to balance revenue objectives, customer requirements, and legal and business risk.

  • Build and maintain contract templates, negotiation playbooks, approval thresholds, and fallback positions that allow the company to scale contracting efficiently.

  • Evaluate and implement systems and processes to improve contract intake, negotiation, approval, execution, and management.

Privacy, Data & Security

  • Draft and negotiate data processing agreements, privacy terms, and security addenda.

  • Advise on issues including breach notification, data residency, subprocessors, data retention and deletion, customer data usage, and AI-related restrictions.

  • Review and structure third-party data-sharing arrangements, including arrangements involving customers, technology partners, custodians, and other data providers.

  • Partner with Product, Engineering, and Security on the legal implications of new products, integrations, data flows, and AI/ML functionality.

  • Support enterprise security reviews and the legal components of SOC 2, ISO 27001, and related compliance processes.

  • Help establish scalable approaches to customer requirements concerning AI, customer data usage, and restrictions on the use of confidential or personal information.

Employment & General Corporate Matters

  • Provide practical legal support on routine employment matters, including offer letters, contractor and consulting agreements, confidentiality and invention assignment agreements, and employee separations.

  • Review and negotiate vendor, partnership, and other operational agreements.

  • Identify matters requiring specialized expertise and efficiently scope and manage outside counsel.

  • Transition appropriate work from outside counsel to the internal legal function over time while maintaining strong outside-counsel relationships for specialized matters.

What We're Looking For

Required Qualifications

  • JD from a top law school.

  • Active membership in good standing with the bar of at least one U.S. jurisdiction.

  • 5–15 years of legal experience.

  • At least 3 years of in-house experience, including direct ownership of commercial contracting.

  • Law firm training in technology transactions, commercial contracts, privacy, or a closely related practice area.

  • Direct experience negotiating MSAs, order forms, and multi-year enterprise agreements for a B2B SaaS company.

  • Direct experience negotiating DPAs and security addenda, including provisions relating to:

    • breach notification;

    • data residency;

    • subprocessors;

    • data retention and deletion; and

    • AI usage and model-training restrictions.

  • Experience reviewing and structuring third-party data-sharing arrangements.

  • General employment law experience, including offer letters, contractor and consulting agreements, and employee separations.

  • Experience determining when specialized legal advice is required and scoping and managing outside counsel.

  • Experience working at a company that had fewer than 250 employees when you joined, or that was Series C or earlier.

  • Strong business judgment and the ability to distinguish material risk from theoretical risk.

  • Ability to operate independently, prioritize competing demands, and provide clear recommendations rather than simply identifying legal issues.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience serving as a company's first legal hire.

  • Experience transitioning significant legal responsibilities from outside counsel to an internal legal function.

  • Experience building contract templates, negotiation playbooks, approval frameworks, and fallback positions from the ground up.

  • Working knowledge of the financial services ecosystem, including wealth managers, asset managers, custodians, and the relationships among them.

  • Experience supporting SOC 2, ISO 27001, enterprise security reviews, or related compliance programs.

  • Experience evaluating, selecting, or implementing contract lifecycle management software.

We're a Series D company with $325M+ in funding (a16z, Accel, Spark Capital, etc.), looking for exceptional people to help us achieve this mission. We want your time here to be the most meaningful experience of your career. Join us, and help change mental healthcare for the better.

As Counsel, Corporate & Risk, you will be a key strategic partner to Headway’s Procurement, Finance, Customer Experience, and Communications teams during a pivotal growth phase for the company. At Beyond Finance, we've made it our mission to help everyday Americans escape the endless cycle of crippling debt and step into a brighter financial future. Through compassionate, individualized care, a culture focused on compliance and ethics, supportive user-centric technology, and customized financial solutions, we've helped over 1 million clients on their path to a brighter future.

While we're proud of what we've already accomplished, we're searching for new collaborators to help us get to the next level! If you're looking to join a forward-thinking, rapidly growing organization with helping people as its number one goal, we want to hear from you.

About the Role

Our Negotiations Escalations Specialists play a key role in the success of our clients becoming free of debt. Working on behalf of clients, you will coordinate efforts to help negotiate delinquent accounts placed with Law Firms for the best possible savings.

This role requires the judgment to interpret legal correspondence — summonses, complaints, and settlement demands — and translate it into an informed negotiation strategy, all while operating within a strict regulatory and compliance framework. The ideal candidate is a sharp communicator and relationship-builder who is comfortable working under legal deadlines and pressure, and who takes real satisfaction in helping clients move toward financial freedom.

What You’ll Do

  • Establish and maintain strong relationships with attorneys and paralegals at Law Firms to effectively negotiate delinquent accounts on behalf of clients to cease further legal action.
  • Manage a portfolio of accounts simultaneously — including escalated portfolios with active lawsuits or imminent legal action
  • Utilize various tools and resources to consolidate common debts from multiple clients, enhancing negotiation leverage with agencies.
  • Secure favorable terms including reduced balances, extended payment timelines, or lump-sum discounts.
  • Demonstrate excellent time management and multitasking skills to efficiently manage account queues.
  • Handle approximately 25-35 outbound/inbound calls daily (minimum of 4 hours a day of on the phone time)
  • Review legal documents (such as summons, complaints, and settlement demands) to determine legal status and to confirm settlement status.
  • Consistently exhibit a genuine passion for helping others, with a strong focus on meeting clients' needs.
  • Participate in additional duties and special projects as required.
  • Consistently meet or exceed monthly settlement and compliance goals.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field (e.g., Business Administration, Finance, Banking, Actuarial Science) or relevant work experience is preferred.
  • Exceptional communication skills, including listening, verbal, and written abilities.
  • Proven success working in a metrics-driven, KPI focused environment is preferred.
  • Ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment.
  • Strong commitment to teamwork, collaboration, and fostering an inclusive environment.
  • A deep passion for assisting others, with a client-focused approach.
  • Proficiency in technology; experience with Salesforce or similar CRM systems is a plus.

The base salary range represents the anticipated salary range for this position. The actual base salary offered within the range will depend on numerous factors including the individual’s skills, experience, performance, and the location where work is performed. In addition to base salary, this position qualifies for commission. Negotiation Specialists earn a monthly commission based on the amount of debt negotiated subject to the terms outlined in the company's commission plan. Full-time employees hired into this position are eligible for health care benefits shown here.

Base Salary Range

$21—$21 USD

Why Join Us?

While you make a difference for others, we’ll work to make a difference for you, providing an uplifting, collaborative work environment and benefits that reflect your value to us. For eligible full-time employees, we offer:

  • Considerable employer contributions for health, dental, and vision programs
  • Generous PTO, paid holidays, and paid parental leave
  • 401(k) matching program
  • Merit advancement opportunities
  • Career development & training

And finally, our team spirit and culture! We cultivate an environment of community, connection, and belonging across our entire organization.

No placement fee will be paid to any third party unless such a request has been made by the Beyond HR team.

Who is Tenable?

Tenable® is the Exposure Management company. Over 40,000 organizations around the globe rely on Tenable to understand and reduce cyber risk. Our global employees support 65 percent of the Fortune 500, 50 percent of the Global 2000, and large government agencies. Come be part of our journey!

What makes Tenable such a great place to work?

Ask a member of our team and they’ll answer, “Our people!” We work together to build and innovate best-in-class cybersecurity solutions for our customers; all while creating a culture of belonging, respect, and excellence where we can be our best selves. When you’re part of our #OneTenable team, you can expect to partner with some of the most talented and passionate people in the industry, and have the support and resources you need to do work that truly matters. We deliver results that exceed expectations and we win together!

Your Role:

Tenable’s Director, Global Government Affairs (SLED) represents Tenable before state and local legislators, Chief Information Officers (CIOs), Chief Information Security Officers (CISOs), procurement officials, and education leaders, as well as across national SLED organizations, trade associations, and coalitions.

This position develops and executes comprehensive state and local advocacy strategies in tight alignment with Tenable’s SLED sales and business development leadership. A core element of the role involves monitoring state policy developments, managing contract lobbyists in target jurisdictions, and turning association and legislative intelligence into actionable growth strategies for field sales teams.

Your Opportunity:

  • Public Sector Business Enablement: Partner closely with SLED territory sales teams and sales leadership to open doors, navigate procurement cycles, and highlight the operational value of exposure management solutions to state and local leaders.
  • Consultant & Lobbyist Management: Directly direct and manage outside government relations consultants and contract lobbyists in key priority states (including California, Texas, New York, and Florida), setting priorities and ensuring measurable results.
  • Trade Association & Coalition Leadership: Represent Tenable within key technology associations and national SLED bodies (e.g., NASCIO, NGA). Actively monitor state legislative trends and translate association briefings into timely, actionable commercial intelligence for regional sales teams.
  • Executive Relationship Building: Cultivate and sustain deep, credible relationships with state CIOs, CISOs, state agency technology leaders, and key procurement decision-makers nationwide.
  • Policy Strategy & Legislative Tracking: Track, evaluate, and influence state and local legislation and executive policies impacting cybersecurity standards, AI adoption, and public sector risk management.
  • Ethics & Lobbying Compliance: Navigate state-specific lobbying rules, gift restrictions, and disclosure requirements in close coordination with Tenable legal and compliance teams.
  • Solution Advocacy: Develop and maintain a thorough understanding of Tenable’s exposure management platform and its application to state, local, and higher education operational resilience.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Align government affairs strategies with product marketing, corporate communications, and executive leadership priorities.

What You’ll Need:

  • Minimum of 7+ years of relevant experience in state and local government affairs, public policy, state agency administration, or SLED business development, with demonstrated leadership experience.
  • Proven track record establishing credibility and working relationships with state and local CIOs, CISOs, IT procurement officials, and legislative staff.
  • Demonstrated experience managing external government affairs consultants and contract lobbyists to achieve targeted policy and business outcomes.
  • Strong working knowledge of state legislative processes, budget appropriation cycles, and public sector acquisition vehicles.
  • Demonstrated success leveraging national intergovernmental organizations and trade associations to represent company priorities.
  • Exceptional written, verbal, and executive presentation skills, with the ability to convey complex policy topics to commercial sales teams and government executives alike.
  • Travel: Domestic travel required, typically monthly to quarterly depending on state legislative calendars, major SLED conferences, and jurisdictional priorities.
  • Availability: Planned position start date of March 2027.
  • Bachelor’s degree required.

And Ideally:

  • Working familiarity with cybersecurity principles, IT infrastructure, enterprise software, or AI policy (formal cybersecurity industry experience is not required; domain-specific exposure management solutions can be learned on the job).
  • Prior service as a state Chief Information Officer (CIO), Chief Information Security Officer (CISO), Deputy CIO/CISO, or senior state technology leader.
  • Direct experience overseeing legislative or consulting engagements in including California, Texas, New York, or Florida.
  • Experience serving as an intelligence bridge between public sector associations and quota-carrying sales representatives to accelerate pipeline generation.
  • Advanced degree in Public Policy, Public Administration, Political Science, Law, or a related field.

Employees are also eligible for variable compensation in addition to base pay (commission for sales roles, bonus for non-sales roles), depending on company and individual performance. About the Role

The Ascend Residency is a highly competitive paid leadership role within Alma's peer community for in-house immigration professionals. Each month, one Resident is selected to shape the community conversation, surface what matters most to the field, and make Ascend materially more valuable for immigration leaders across companies.

Residents are selected based on the strength of their professional experience, credibility in the immigration field, demonstrated judgment, and ability to contribute original thought leadership to the community.

This is not an ambassador title or a visibility play. It is a substantive working role for an immigration leader with real operating experience, a sharp perspective, and something valuable to contribute to peers.

What You'll Do

  • Design and host 1 webinar on a topic the immigration community is actively wrestling with (Alma handles promotion and logistics)

  • Design and host 1 sponsored in-person event (Alma funds and supports)

  • Publish 3-4 original posts or insights on policy, compliance, AI tools, vendor strategy, or program design

  • Create 1 durable resource (framework, template, playbook, or briefing) aligned with Alma

  • Spark and sustain peer conversations across the community

What You'll Receive

  • $8,000 honorarium, paid at end of the residency month; 5-10 hours/week

  • Production, scheduling, logistics, and promotion support from Alma

  • Sponsored in-person event designed with you and funded by Alma

  • Permanent recognition as an Ascend Resident and entry into the Ascend Alumni network

  • Priority consideration for future speaking, editorial, and community partnership opportunities

Who This Is For

  • In-house immigration program managers, directors, and leads

  • Global mobility professionals with meaningful immigration program ownership.

  • Practitioners who manage stakeholders, policy, compliance, vendors, employee experience, and program design.

  • Operators with a clear point of view on where immigration practice, compliance, and technology are heading.

  • Immigration leaders who are respected by peers and can bring thoughtful, practical, field-tested insights to the community.

Who This Is Not For

  • General HR or People Ops professionals without direct immigration program responsibility

  • Community managers or marketers seeking visibility opportunities

  • Professionals adjacent to immigration who do not actively run or advise on the program

  • Applicants who are not prepared to contribute original thinking, practical resources, and meaningful peer engagement.

How to Apply

Applications take approximately 20 minutes. Please respond to the following:

  1. What are the 2-3 highest-leverage contributions you would make during your Residency month, and how would you judge whether they were useful?

  2. What topic would you choose for your webinar or live exchange, and why is it timely for in-house immigration leaders right now?

  3. What is one example of the kind of framework, post, briefing, or resource you would create for the community library?

  4. Who are the immigration professionals you would want to bring into Ascend, and why would they trust your invitation?

Selection Process

Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. Residents are selected based on professional experience, demonstrated immigration program leadership, quality of thought leadership and strength of proposed contributions.

Please note: This is an independent contractor (1099) role.
